newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said the EU health ministers who met last Friday in Adare, Ireland, discussed blood self-sufficiency within the EU. Since no harmonisation has been achieved in this sector, the EU is now facing a blood shortage and Germany, Italy and Spain imported blood from the United States, she said.

To promote self-sufficiency inside the Union, confidence in the entire bloodchain needed to be improved, she said. She said the conclusions of the meeting were available in her office and that the issue would be discussed during the Health Council on November 12.

Asked about discussions during the informal General Affairs Council in Tralee of the EU-U.S. conflict over the Helms-Burton legislation, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Council would not implement retaliatory measures before the beginning of October since there was no apparent hurry. He also said that cases of European individuals or companies being affected by the American law would not arise before the U.S. presidential elections.
Spokesman Peter Guilford added that neither the Commission nor Council had decided to delay escalating the dispute in the World Trade Organisation until after the elections.

In answer to a question, Guilford said that restrictions on entry of U.S. citizens into the EU had never been part of the blocking statute but that one of the other three related proposals concerned possible visa restrictions. He added that a Council working group was meeting on the blocking legislation today.
Van der Pas said that the issue of Public Services was on the provisional agenda of Wednesday's Commission meeting.

Spokesman Gerry Kiely said the Scientific Veterinary Committee had decided on Friday to create two subgroups -- one on research in general, the second to evaluate if maternal transmission of BSE affected milk.
Kiely said that there would not be many issues related to BSE on the agenda of Wednesday's Standing Veterinary Committee.
